[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Robert Glasgow married [[Jack-2557|Elizabeth Jack (abt.1771-abt.1802)]].<ref>"Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers - Banns and Marriages," database, National Records of Scotland, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople] (accessed 19 April 2025), Robert Glasgow marriage to Elizabeth Jack on or after 31 May 1789 in Barony, Lanarkshire, Scotland; citing Parish Number 622, Ref 70/79, Frame 1769.</ref>

His wife Elizabeth passed away in 1802. <ref>"Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers - Deaths and Burials," database, National Records of Scotland, ScotlandsPeople (accessed 19 April 2025), Elizabeth Jack death or burial (died age 38) on 18 Nov 1802 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland; citing Parish Number 644/1, Ref 640/107.</ref>

He remarried to Margaret Brash 06 Nov 1803 in Barony. <ref> "Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers - Banns and Marriages," database, National Records of Scotland, ScotlandsPeople (accessed 19 April 2025), Margaret Brash marriage to Robert Glasgow on or after 6 Nov 1803 in Barony, Lanarkshire, Scotland; citing Parish Number 622, Ref 70/252, Frame 1858.</ref>

Robert (age 79), weaver, died or was buried on 9 September 1839 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland.<ref>"Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers - Deaths and Burials," database, National Records of Scotland, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople] (accessed 19 April 2025), Robert Glasgow death or burial (died age 79) on 9 Sep 1839 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland; citing Parish Number 644/1, Ref 670/67.</ref>


== Research Notes ==
=== Additional parish and later-life evidence ===
Robert Glasgow baptised 17 February 1760 at Wandell and Lamington, James Glasgow and Marion Saidler. The record-defined child is represented by Glasgow-1530; Glasgow-1538 is a qualified adult comparison with separate family hypotheses and a competing 1784 index. Do not merge these accounts. Preserve paternal assessments 84% and 62%, current vital bounds and maternal uncertainty; Saidler/Sadler is retained as a recorded-name variation, not independent proof. Inspected Findmypast derivative; original register or memorial uninspected. No new person, attachment or relationship-confidence change.

Robert Glasgow, weaver of Calton, Glasgow, aged 79: the OPR derivative labels 9 September 1839 as Death date (OPR 644/67 item 3 page 127), while the companion labels it Burial date and leaves death incomplete. This matches the existing record-defined Glasgow-1530 account, but the label discrepancy prevents upgrading its before-9-September death bound to an exact death day. Birth 1760 is age-derived; no merge with Glasgow-1538 or parent-confidence change. Inspected Findmypast derivative; original register or memorial uninspected. No new person, attachment or relationship-confidence change.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1120]] is assessed at 84% (probable). The age79 burial in 1839 favours the 1760 child over the 1755 and 1758 candidates. That child’s Wandell/Lamington index names James Glasgow and Marion Saidler; the maintained older-widower adult sequence is compatible with that exact generation.

Complete father proposition84%; the child-to-widower identity is inferred and Robert-1538 remains a separate overlapping account. No alternative birth is deleted.

Next useful test: Use residence, occupation or family witnesses to distinguish the three Robert childhoods.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTFT-KJ9 FamilySearch, Scotland Births and Baptisms: Robert Glasgow, 17 February 1760, Wandell and Lamington; James Glasgow and Marion Saidler (maintained index citation)]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Robert and Margaret Brash ===

[[Glasgow-1538|Robert Glasgow, Margaret Brash’s husband]], may be the same adult as [[Glasgow-1530|Robert Glasgow]]. The older widower sequence and age-79 burial favour the 1760 Wandell and Lamington child. James Glasgow and Marion Saidler are selected as probable parents of Robert-1538, 62% each, dependent on that unresolved identity chain. This does not prove two distinct sons named Robert, reconcile Robert’s competing births, or establish James’s own childhood. The baptism names Marion independently; her motherhood is not inferred merely from a spouse attachment.<ref>“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTFT-KJ9 Robert Glasgow, 17 February 1760], Wandell and Lamington, Lanarkshire; parents James Glasgow and Marion Saidler. Existing indexed citation reused; original image not newly inspected.</ref>


=== Named parents in three civil events — 30 October 2026 ===

Alexander’s marriages in1861and1867and death in1875 consistently name his parents [[Glasgow-1538|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Brash-171|Margaret Brash]]. The same ages, flesher trade and successive wives identify one adult:48 in1861,54 in1867and62 in1875. His existing father is assessed at99%, increased from97%; his already named mother receives her first individual99% assessment. This does not settle Robert’s own1760/1784 childhood alternatives or his62%James Glasgow parent hypothesis.

On30April1861, Alexander,48, widowed and a flesher, married [[Bicket-53|Elizabeth Bicket]],42.<ref>FamilySearch, “Scotland, Civil Registration,1855–1875,1881,1891,” [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLR-J1JQ Robert Glasgow in entry for Alexr Glasgow,30April1861]; displayed derivative index inspected30October2026. Father Robert and mother Margaret Brash Glasgow; earlier Calton reference644/4/154 retained. The original certificate was not inspected.</ref>

On23April1867, Alexander,54, widowed and a master flesher, married [[Smith-231676|Janet Smith]],46.<ref>FamilySearch, “Scotland, Civil Registration,1855–1875,1881,1891,” [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TPS-Q18Q Robert Glasgow in entry for Alexr Glasgow,23April1867]; displayed derivative index inspected30October2026. Original uninspected. The same full parental couple is indexed.</ref> The bride is strongly identified with his1871wife Janet by name, husband and compatible age.

Alexander’s death is explicitly indexed on4October1875at Rothesay, Buteshire. He was62, married and a flesher; the same parents are named. Janet Smith appears under Other People, whose label alone does not define her role.<ref>FamilySearch, “Scotland, Civil Registration,1855–1875,1881,1891,” [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSF1-N2WT Robert Glasgow in entry for Alexander Glasgow,4October1875]; displayed derivative index inspected30October2026. Original image requires a FamilySearch centre or affiliate library. Rothesay is the indexed event/registration place, not a verified exact death address.</ref>

The inspected sources are provider indexes. Multiple person rows for one event are not independent evidence; the originals and informants have not been read. The Ancestry burial database title1655–1854 does not itself explain an1875entry, and Elizabeth’s separate1866death citation does not name Alexander’s father. These sources remain identifiable below, with the civil indexes supplying the current parental argument. FamilySearch tree attachments are comparisons, not proof of Robert’s1760birth.
